newsitem.title: ROMANIA: World Bank mission to Romania to assess economy.
newsitem.headline: World Bank mission to Romania to assess economy.

text.p: A senior World Bank mission met Romania's Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea on Monday to discuss the new centrist coalition's government programme.

A government statement said Ciorbea, seeking financial support from the World Bank, had detailed top policy priorities of his cabinet which took over after leftists were ousted in elections last November.
It said Kenneth Lay, the Bank's representative for Europe and Asia, who heads the mission to Bucharest said his institution would support the reform programme, including the social sector.
Last year the World Bank continued its infrastructure and other project loans to Romania, although the IMF froze credits over slow economic reform in the Balkan country.
But the Bank withheld the final tranche of about $80 million under a $280 million Financial and Enterprise Sector Adjustment Loan (FESAL) due in the last quarter of 1996.
The IMF suspended three-year standby credits worth $460 million, the third package agreed with post-communist Romania, which drew only up to one-third of the total sum.

Romania ranks as the World Bank's second-largest borrower in Eastern Europe, receiving some $510 million in committments for structural adjustment, infrastructure and social and private sector programmes in fiscal year 1996.
